Language reference

A typed language with .pac at its core.

Learn the syntax and types that the current compiler actually accepts, plus the boundaries that remain future work.

The implemented language core

The current v0.1 language is deliberately smaller than the long-term design.

.pac

Source and grammar

Modules, imports of built-in namespaces, structs, functions, expressions, loops, errors and capability declarations.

Static subset

Types

Int, Float, Bool, String, Unit, List, tensors, nominal structs and opaque engine types; no user-defined generics yet.

PE1xxx–PE7xxx

Diagnostics

Source spans, stable diagnostic codes, error recovery in the Python parser and targeted type/capability messages.

List<T>

Collections

Mutable lists, indexing and common list operations exist. Unicode and iterator APIs remain limited.

Start with ordinary code

The build pipeline consumes this actual PEACOCK source file; it is not Python in a renamed file.

// The smallest PEACOCK program.
module hello

fn main() -> Unit {
    print("Hello from PEACOCK");
}
Explicit

No implicit numeric coercion

Int and Float are distinct; write an explicit conversion rather than relying on silent widening.

Declared + granted

Capability-gated effects

Filesystem, compute and UI authority are declared in source and granted independently by the host.

Read a wider syntax tour

The tour exercises functions, expressions, lists, structs, control flow and error handling in the supported grammar.

examples/tour.pac

Selectable source — use your browser's copy command. · SHA-256: 4aefd4c27e94bb02

// PEACOCK language tour: functions, structs, lists, loops, errors, assertions.
module tour

struct Point {
    x: Int
    y: Int
}

fn distance_squared(a: Point, b: Point) -> Int {
    let dx = a.x - b.x;
    let dy = a.y - b.y;
    return dx * dx + dy * dy;
}

fn sum(values: List<Int>) -> Int {
    let mut total = 0;
    for value in values {
        total += value;
    }
    return total;
}

fn doubled(n: Int) -> Int {
    if n < 0 {
        throw "doubled() does not accept negative numbers";
    }
    return n * 2;
}

fn main() -> Unit {
    let mut squares: List<Int> = [];
    for i in 1..6 {
        squares.push(i * i);
    }
    print("squares: " + str(squares));
    print("sum: " + str(sum(squares)));

    let origin = Point(0, 0);
    let corner = Point(3, 4);
    print("distance squared: " + str(distance_squared(origin, corner)));

    let mut i = 0;
    while i < 3 {
        print("loop " + str(i));
        i += 1;
    }

    try {
        print("doubled: " + str(doubled(21)));
        let bad = doubled(-1);
        print("not reached " + str(bad));
    } catch (message) {
        print("caught: " + message);
    }

    assert(sum(squares) == 55, "sum of squares should be 55");

    let label = "  PEACOCK  ";
    print("trimmed: [" + label.trim() + "]");
    print("characters: " + str(len(label)));
    print("split: " + str("a,b,c".split(",")));
    print("types: " + type_name(label) + ", " + type_name(3.5) + ", " + type_name(squares));
}
